correctness.rationale: For all admissible geometric parameters, disjoint branch sets imply genus five and a 2-primary quotient isogeny, preserving 3-divisible groups. Elliptic Hasse scalars are 0 and -u. The genus-three Cartier coefficient matrix has rank exactly two; the triple twisted product explicitly factors through T and has rank zero exactly when T=0, otherwise stable rank two. Thus both invariants follow without extrapolating finite tests. Rank-zero equations reduce to t=-s and s^4=-1; the four roots are simple and inversion/swap connect their curves. Independently executable standard-library verifier checks sparse identities and all 42 admissible ordered GF9 pairs.

value.rationale: The two-dimensional symmetric (1,1,0) Howe family is natural because it fixes the characteristic-three supersingular elliptic double cover and imposes x↦-x stability on the other branch set. The result gives all four 3-rank/a-number strata and finds the zero-rank locus as four transverse parameter points with a single geometric curve. These exact arithmetic boundaries are not supplied by the general Richelot decomposition or genus-five sextic equation construction and meaningfully inform the search for nonordinary genus-five Jacobians.
